Johnny Cash, and this song, mean a lot to me, so have some info.

In '97, he developed a disease that kept him from touring. He was misdiagnosed twice, preventing proper treatment., but that disease was dysautonomia. It causes your automatic nervous system to falter, stopping proper signaling from your brain and spinal cord to your organs.

Note the opening lyrics to the song:

I hurt myself today
to see if I still feel

That lyric has the same metaphorical meaning of the original, but to Johnny Cash, it meant something more. His disease had literally put him in a position where had to wake up every day, wondering if he still had the ability to feel. In 2002, when this cover was released, he'd lived with dysautonomia for 5 years. That's likely why he wanted to cover it in the first place.

Even more heartbreaking is that in 2003, when the video was recorded, you see him and his long-time wife June Carter Cash. She passes away 3 months after recording. Having lost the love of his life, Johnny Cash loses the will to live. His disease worsens rapidly, and he follows her to the grave just 4 months later on September 12, 2003.

So imagine actually paying remembrance and mourning slightly for 9/11, waking up the next day, and then learning Johnny Cash died of a broken heart. I might've cried more than when 9/11 was actually happening. You get the news, the song starts playing in your head, you put on your headphones to actually listen, fucking waterworks.
Thank you for posting this. I love his music and learned a little about him through the stories and songs but never knew what the circumstances were around their passing.

I really can't decide which version I like better, though I'll argue that both versions, despite having the same lyrics, can be interpreted differently simply because of who is singing each one. The original seems to deal with depression and loneliness, and the "hurt" comes from physical self-harm; Cash's version seems to deal with regrets, growing old and the loss of loved ones, and the "hurt" comes from remembering the past.
